newsitem.title: UK: BOE sees little cause for concern over City future.
newsitem.headline: BOE sees little cause for concern over City future.

text.p: The Bank of England sees little cause for concern about London losing its role as a major international finance centre if Britain does not join European monetary union, executive director Ian Plenderleith said.
In a speech prepared for delivery at the City of London Central Banking Conference, he said he understood why general concerns of this sort were being expressed.
"But when you look specifically at precisely how it is feared London might suffer, as we at the Bank have, it is in fact very hard to see where concrete grounds arise for concern," Plenderleith said.
He cited six reasons why London could be confident of maintaining its role if Britain did not join a single currency:

- London is an important focus of business for other regions such as North America, the Middle and Far East, emerging market economies, central and eastern Europe and Latin America. "London's global, international role should not be called into question by European monetary union."
- The modernisation of continental European financial centres, far from diverting business from London, has generated additional business.
- Financial institutions continue to show a preference for setting up or centralising operations in London despite uncertainty about Britain's participation in EMU.
- Monetary union will not alter the basic economics of international financial activity, which continues to point towards concentration in one centre, with London clearly the preferred choice.

- London's distinctive strengths will remain in place -- the English language, the convenient time zone, the availability of relevant trading and banking skills, the regulatory framework, the technological infrastructure and the existing "critical mass" of markets and services.
- Major advances continue to be made in improving the infrastructure.
Plenderleith said these were very strong reasons for not writing off prematurely London's pre-eminent international position "which I can assure you we have no intention of allowing to be eroded."
